title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA ADDRESSES MEMBERS OF THE INDIAN COMMUNITY IN ROMANIA
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau President's Secretariat PRESIDENT OF INDIA ADDRESSES MEMBERS OF THE INDIAN COMMUNITY IN ROMANIA STRONGEST PILLAR OF INDIA–ROMANIA RELATIONS IS THE CLOSE BOND BETWEEN OUR PEOPLES: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU PRESIDENT URGES THE INDIAN COMMUNITY IN ROMANIA TO CONTINUE BEING ACTIVE PARTNERS IN THE DEVELOPMENTAL JOURNEY OF INDIA प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 JUL 2026 7:07PM by PIB Delhi On the concluding day (July 25, 2026) of her State visit to Romania, the President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu addressed the members of the Indian Community and ‘Friends of India’ at a Reception hosted by the Ambassador of India to Romania Bucharest. The accompanying Minister of State for Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution Smt Nimuben Jayantibhai Bambhaniya and Members of Parliament Dr. Dinesh Sharma and Shri Vijay Baghel were also present on the occasion. Addressing the enthusiastic gathering of the Indian community living in Romania, the President said that even though they live far away from India, they remain deeply connected to their motherland. Their achievements and love for India make every Indian proud. She was happy to note that Indian companies and Indian professionals are making significant contributions to Romania’s development while also creating new opportunities for cooperation between our two countries. The President said that the strongest pillar of India–Romania relations is the close bond between our peoples. She was happy to note that the Indian diaspora remains united, keeping India’s rich cultural heritage alive in Romania and a new generation of Indian IT engineers, scholars, researchers, health care professionals and students is now making Romania their home. The President said that the contribution of the Indian community to Romania’s economy and society, and their efforts to promote Indian culture and values in Romania, make them true representatives of India. Through their hard work, talent and dedication, members of the Indian community have achieved remarkable success. She appreciated the Government and people of Romania for welcoming the Indian community and ensuring their safety. The President said that our vision of ‘Viksit Bharat 2047’ is to build a prosperous, modern, self-reliant and inclusive India. She urged the Indian community in Romania to continue being active partners in the developmental journey of India. She underlined that their experience, expertise and achievements will contribute to the progress of our nation. The President appreciated Romanian ‘Friends of India’ who are present at the Reception. She said that their love for Indian art and culture, as well as their spiritual connections with India, form an important bridge bringing our people together. She acknowledged their continued support in further strengthening the bonds of friendship and cooperation between India and Romania. After the successful completion of the three-nation State visit, the President departed for New Delhi. title: Prime Minister expresses delight as Sarnath is inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List
content:

                25 JUL 2026 7:05PM by PIB Delhi Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today expressed that it is a proud moment for every Indian, sharing his delight that Sarnath in Uttar Pradesh has been inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List. title: Public Advisory: Beware of Fraudulent Air Suvidha 2.0 Websites
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Civil Aviation Public Advisory: Beware of Fraudulent Air Suvidha 2.0 Websites प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 JUL 2026 3:59PM by PIB Delhi It has come to the notice of the Ministry of Civil Aviation that certain fraudulent websites and portals are impersonating Air Suvidha 2.0 and misleading passengers by redirecting them to payment gateways. Passengers are advised that Air Suvidha 2.0 services are provided free of cost, and no payment is required for submission of the Self-Declaration Form. The only official Air Suvidha 2.0 portal is: https://airsuvidha.civilaviation.gov.in/ Passengers are urged to verify the website URL carefully before sharing any personal or travel-related information and to avoid making payments on any unauthorized website claiming to offer Air Suvidha 2.0 services. Passengers are requested to use only the official portal and rely on official Government communications for authentic information. Issued in the interest of passenger awareness and public safety. **** Divyanshu Kumar (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289355) आगंतुक पटल  : 286 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , Marathi , हिन्दी , Bengali , Gujarati , Tamil , Malayalam Ministry of Civil Aviation Public Advisory: Beware of Fraudulent Air Suvidha 2.0 Websites प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: “Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath” Inscribed in the UNESCO World Heritage List
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Culture “Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath” Inscribed in the UNESCO World Heritage List प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 JUL 2026 6:04PM by PIB Delhi Today, in a remarkable decision taken at the 48 th Session of the World Heritage Committee being held at Busan, South Korea, India’s official nomination for 2025-26 cycle, “Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath” got inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List, becoming India’s 45th property to receive this recognition. This global accolade celebrates India’s enduring cultural legacy, showcasing its diverse traditions of architectural brilliance, regional identity, and historical continuity. Tweet by UNESCO/Hon’ble HCM/Hon’ble PM Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Hon’ble Union Minister of Culture Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat along with Hon’ble Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh Shri Yogi Adityanath lauded the historic milestone and congratulated the people of India for this achievement. Indian Delegation giving thanks speech at 48 th COM at Busan Ancient Buddhist Site, Sarnath The inscribed serial property comprises two component parts – Chaukhandi Stupa and the Archaeological Remains of Sarnath (Dhamekh Stupa, Dharmrajika Stupa, Mulagandgakuti Vihara, Ashokan Pillar, etc.) – located within Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh. Together these two components preserve the architectural and archaeological remains of the ancient site of Sarnath, known in the Buddhist tradition under different names – Rishipatana, Ishipatana, Mrigadava. They all refer to a sacred geography, where the Buddha visited in the 6th century BCE and delivered his first sermon known as the “Turning of the Wheel of the Law” ( Dharmachakra pravartana ). This event marked the inception of the Buddhist sangha and the establishment of the principles of the Noble Eightfold Path. Indicated by the Buddha himself to be one of the four key sites of Buddhist pilgrimage, Sarnath developed over centuries through royal, monastic and lay patronage. Numerous stupas, temples and viharas were constructed around what is believed to be the place of the first sermon of Gautama Buddha and the site where he met his first disciples. Having seen decline in the 12th century CE and subsequent destruction, it fell into obscurity until its re-discovery in the 18th century. The site comprises an ensemble of ancient monuments constructed from the pre-Mauryan period (5th-4th centuries BCE to 3rd century BCE) up until the destruction of Sarnath in the 12th century CE (with some later additions). Sarnath has been one of the most extensively excavated sites by the Archaeological Survey of India which resulted in a stratified settlement spread across 16 centuries (5th-4th centuries BCE to 12th century CE). Excavations at the Archaeological remains of Sarnath, 1907-1908 (Source-Archaeological Survey of India) After the declaration of Sarnath as the World Heritage Property, three of the four most significant Buddhist Pilgrim sites; i.e. Lumbini (Nepal), Mahabodhi Temple, Bodhgaya (Bihar) and now Sarnath (Uttar Pradesh) are now included in the World Heritage, along with several other important Buddhist sites such as Sanchi, Nalanda, Ajanta (all three in India), Anuradhapur (Sri Lanka) Paharpur (Bangladesh), Taxila and Takht-i-Bahi (both in present day Pakistan), etc. Sarnath as a UNESCO World Heritage Property The ancient site of Sarnath was included in the Tentative List of World Heritage in 1998. The proposal to include the site in the list of World Heritage was sent to the consideration of World Heritage Committee in Jan 2025 and after a rigorous eighteen-month long process involving several technical meetings with the advisory bodies and visit of ICOMOS’s mission to review the site, this historic decision was taken by the members of the World Heritage Committee today evening at Busan, South Korea. ICOMOS technical evaluation mission examining the excavated staircase at Sarnath during 24 to 29 September 2025 Bird-eye view of the Excavated remains at Sarnath (Source-Archaeological Survey of India) During the Committee Meeting, the 21 Members of the World Heritage Committee, Member States, UNESCO Secretariat, World Heritage Centre, and Advisory Bodies of UNESCO (ICOMOS, IUCN, ICCROM) congratulated the delegation of India for this momentous occasion. The “Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath” is nominated under criteria (iii) and (vi), recognizing enduring spiritual significance of Sarnath Cr. (iii) , one of the four principal destinations of Buddhist pilgrimage, as demonstrated by the large number of religious buildings and other monuments that were built and rebuilt on-site during the many centuries of its existence and through Cr.(vi) direct and tangible way to the events in the life of the Buddha that are of outstanding significance to the Buddhist community – his first sermon and meeting of his first disciples. The importance of these events and their meaning is carried by the numerous constructions erected at Sarnath over the centuries, which are a response to the message of the Buddha, his teachings, and the concept of Triratna . View of excavated Ashoka pillar and Lion Capital with the Mulagandhakuti Vihara, 1904-06 (Source-Archaeological Survey of India) Excavated Ashokan Lion Capital, 1904-06 later declared as the National Emblem (Source-Archaeological Survey of India) The purpose of including these heritage sites in UNESCO’s list is to preserve and promote shared heritage based on OUVs (Outstanding Universal Values) found in cultural, natural as well as mixed properties across 196 countries. On its part, India became a member of the coveted World Heritage Committee from 2021-25 and also hosted for the first time the World Heritage Committee Meeting in July 2024 at New Delhi. Scientific Preservation Works underway on the brick votive Stupas at Sarnath This global recognition is a testimony to New India’s relentless pursuit of highlighting Bharat’s heritage on the world forum. This recognition underscores the conservation and management efforts of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) in preserving these historic treasures. For over 150 years, the Archaeological Survey of India has been excavating and conserving the Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath, leading to the discovery and identification of Sarnath with the place where Shakyamuni Buddha gave his first Sermon. The famous Mauryan Lion Pillar which later became the National Emblem of India and the Dharkachakrapravartan Buddha from the Classic Gupta Art were found from the excavations which are presently displayed at the India's earliest site Museum which was established in 1904. World Heritage status would reinforce India's identity as the birthplace of Buddhism and enhance cultural diplomacy with nations such as Japan, Thailand, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Cambodia, Vietnam, South Korea, Mongolia, etc. This recognition would further support India's efforts to promote Buddhist heritage as a bridge for international engagement and would also showcase India's expertise in heritage conservation and preparedness in nomination process. Last year, ‘the Maratha Military Landscapes of India’ were inscribed in the World Heritage List at the 47 th Session of the World Heritage Committee held at UNESCO Headquarters at Paris. With 45 sites in the List, India ranks 6th globally and 2nd in Asia Pacific Region for the most number of World Heritage Sites. 196 nations have ratified the World Heritage Convention, 1972. India also has 69 sites in the Tentative List of the World Heritage, which is a mandatory threshold for any site to be considered as a World Heritage property in future. Every year, each State Party may propose just one site for consideration of the World Heritage Committee for inscription to the World Heritage List. On behalf of the Government of India, Archaeological Survey of India is the nodal agency of all the World Heritage related matters in the country. With this global recognition, India affirms its commitment to protect Sarnath's Outstanding Universal Value by Manage tourism sustainably and prevent unplanned development in the buffer zone in order to preserve authenticity and integrity of the property. *** M Annadurai (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289399) आगंतुक पटल  : 560 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Gujarati , Urdu , Tamil Ministry of Culture “Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath” Inscribed in the UNESCO World Heritage List प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: DRI intensifies crackdown on gold smuggling; seizes 27 kg smuggled gold in intelligence-led nationwide operations; 12 arrested
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Finance DRI intensifies crackdown on gold smuggling; seizes 27 kg smuggled gold in intelligence-led nationwide operations; 12 arrested प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 JUL 2026 4:01PM by PIB Delhi Continuing its sustained crackdown on organised gold smuggling syndicates, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has carried out a series of intelligence-driven operations across the country, resulting in the seizure of over 27 kg foreign-origin smuggled gold and the arrest of 12 persons . The operations exposed sophisticated concealment methods, including concealment inside aircraft lavatories, specially fabricated cavities in vehicles and utensils, and body concealment, highlighting the evolving modus operandi adopted by organised smuggling syndicates. Acting on specific intelligence, DRI officers at Mumbai intercepted three passengers on 23-24.07.2026 arriving from Addis Ababa and, after an extensive search of the aircraft, recovered 6 foreign origin gold bars weighing around 12 kg concealed inside the ceiling panels of the rear lavatory of aircraft. Investigation revealed that the passengers had concealed the gold for subsequent retrieval by airport staff. The gold was seized and all three passengers were arrested. On 23.07.2026 , acting on specific intelligence, officers of DRI intercepted a female passenger travelling on the Brahmaputra Mail in Uttar Pradesh and recovered 42 foreign origin gold bars weighing around 5 kg concealed in a waist belt and inside her handbag. The passenger admitted that the gold had been smuggled into India through Bangladesh. The gold was seized and the passenger was arrested . In another intelligence-led operation at Mumbai Airport during 22-23.07.2026 , DRI officers unearthed a smuggling syndicate again using aircraft lavatories for concealment of gold dust in wax form, which was subsequently retrieved by compromised aircraft cleaning staff. The operation led to the seizure of 3.7 kg gold dust in wax form and the arrest of five persons , including the carrier, cleaning staff, handler and recipient. On 19-20.07.2026 , officers of DRI intercepted a passenger at Kolkata Railway Station and recovered 4.6 kg foreign-origin gold , ingeniously concealed inside specially fabricated utensils. Investigation revealed that the contraband had been smuggled into India through Myanmar. The gold was seized and the passenger arrested. During the week, in two more separate operations, DRI officers at Cochin and Guwahati seized around 2 kg foreign-origin gold . At Cochin Airport, gold concealed inside the body of a passenger arriving from Dubai was recovered, while at Guwahati, gold biscuits concealed inside a specially fabricated cavity in a car were seized. Two persons were arrested in these operations. **** SR/KMN (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289357) आगंतुक पटल  : 318 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Gujarati , Urdu , Marathi , हिन्दी , Tamil Ministry of Finance DRI intensifies crackdown on gold smuggling; seizes 27 kg smuggled gold in intelligence-led nationwide operations; 12 arrested प्रविष्टि तिथि:

On 19-20.07.2026 , officers of DRI intercepted a passenger at Kolkata Railway Station and recovered 4.6 kg foreign-origin gold , ingeniously concealed inside specially fabricated utensils. Investigation revealed that the contraband had been smuggled into India through Myanmar. The gold was seized and the passenger arrested. During the week, in two more separate operations, DRI officers at Cochin and Guwahati seized around 2 kg foreign-origin gold . At Cochin Airport, gold concealed inside the body of a passenger arriving from Dubai was recovered, while at Guwahati, gold biscuits concealed inside a specially fabricated cavity in a car were seized. Two persons were arrested in these operations. **** SR/KMN (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289357)

title: From Mines to Markets: How MoRTH's Kanpur–Kabrai Highway Will Transform Logistics and Agriculture
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Road Transport & Highways From Mines to Markets: How MoRTH's Kanpur–Kabrai Highway Will Transform Logistics and Agriculture प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 JUL 2026 5:40PM by PIB Delhi Kanpur–Kabrai (4/6 Lane Access-Controlled) Highway, approved earlier this month by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), is set to emerge as a transformative infrastructure project for Central India. To be implemented by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH), the 117.7-km greenfield highway, with an estimated cost of ₹7,145 crore, forms a vital part of the Bhopal–Kanpur Economic Corridor. The project will strengthen logistics, enhance industrial connectivity and improve market access for farmers by seamlessly linking Bundelkhand's mineral-rich areas, industrial clusters and agricultural hinterland with major consumption centres. By enabling faster and more efficient movement of minerals, manufactured goods and farm produce, the corridor is expected to reduce logistics costs, improve supply chain efficiency, attract investment, generate employment and drive inclusive regional development. More than a transport corridor, it represents a strategic investment in connecting mines to markets and unlocking Bundelkhand's economic potential. Powering Central India's Logistics Network The Kanpur–Kabrai Highway will significantly improve freight mobility across Bundelkhand by providing a high-speed, access-controlled corridor linking the Kabrai mining belt—one of North India's leading sources of aggregates and construction materials—with major industrial and urban centres, including Kanpur and Bhopal. Faster and more reliable movement of mineral resources will lower transportation costs, reduce fuel consumption and improve operational efficiency for freight operators. The project will also decongest existing highways, enhance the reliability of industrial supply chains and support seamless movement of goods across the region. Travel time between Kanpur and Kabrai is expected to come down from around 3.5 hours to nearly 1.5 hours, improving freight turnaround and strengthening linkages with PM Gati Shakti economic and logistics nodes, thereby creating a stronger foundation for industrial growth and investment. Expanding Market Access for Farmers Beyond strengthening logistics, the highway will improve market access for farmers across Bundelkhand by enabling faster transportation of agricultural produce to mandis, processing units and consumption centres. Shorter travel times will help preserve the quality of perishable commodities, reduce post-harvest losses and lower transportation costs, allowing farmers to realise better value for their produce. The improved corridor will also facilitate easier movement of seeds, fertilisers, farm machinery and other agricultural inputs, enhancing farm productivity while integrating rural producers more closely with regional and national markets. Better connectivity is expected to create new economic opportunities across the agricultural value chain and contribute to higher rural incomes. Driving Regional Prosperity Through Infrastructure The Kanpur–Kabrai Highway reflects MoRTH's commitment to building world-class transport infrastructure that serves as a catalyst for economic transformation. By integrating mining regions, industrial clusters and agricultural hinterlands with major growth centres, the project will strengthen supply chains, improve the ease of doing business and stimulate investment across Bundelkhand. As a critical component of the Bhopal–Kanpur Economic Corridor, it will promote balanced regional development, generate employment and lay the foundation for a more connected, competitive and prosperous Central India. *** GDH/DS (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289391) आगंतुक पटल  : 131 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Tamil Ministry of Road Transport & Highways From Mines to Markets: How MoRTH's Kanpur–Kabrai Highway Will Transform Logistics and Agriculture प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Delhi's Underground Link to the Future: The Tunnel Set to Rewire the Capital's Connectivity
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Road Transport & Highways Delhi's Underground Link to the Future: The Tunnel Set to Rewire the Capital's Connectivity प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 JUL 2026 5:37PM by PIB Delhi For millions arriving in India's capital each year, the first impression of Delhi is often shaped by congested airport approaches, traffic bottlenecks and lengthy journeys between key business, diplomatic and cultural districts. The 6 Lane Dwarka Road Tunnel on NH- 148AE, approved earlier this month by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) is set to redefine urban mobility in the National Capital Region. To be implemented by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH), the 8.1-km, six-lane project, to be developed at an estimated cost of ₹6,969.67 crore on Hybrid Annuity Mode (HAM) under the NH(O) Scheme, will connect the Shiv Murti Interchange on the Dwarka Expressway (NH-248BB) with Nelson Mandela Marg in Vasant Kunj. The corridor will provide a high-speed, access-controlled link between West and South Delhi, particularly benefiting traffic from Gurugram, Dwarka, IGI Airport and West Delhi. Its defining feature is a 3.14-km twin-tube tunnel, including a 1.98-km stretch beneath the Southern Ridge, ensuring seamless mobility while preserving one of Delhi's most ecologically sensitive landscapes. Reimagining Urban Mobility The Dwarka Tunnel Corridor will provide a direct, uninterrupted connection between the Dwarka Expressway and South Delhi, reducing dependence on heavily congested routes such as Dhaula Kuan–IGI Airport–Mahipalpur, Chhatarpur–Mahipalpur and Rangpuri. By improving traffic flow and reducing travel delays, the project will make daily commuting faster, safer and more reliable for residents, airport users and commercial traffic alike. The corridor will also strengthen integration between Delhi and Gurugram, improving access to key residential areas, commercial centres, institutional hubs and the Indira Gandhi International Airport. Together with NHAI's proposed AIIMS–Mahipalpur Elevated Corridor, which will connect the tunnel to the Barapullah Elevated Road, the project will establish seamless east-west connectivity across the city, benefiting travel to East Delhi, Ghaziabad and Noida while creating a more efficient urban transport network. Enhancing Tourism and Visitor Experience Delhi welcomes millions of domestic and international visitors every year, and efficient connectivity is central to their travel experience. The Dwarka Tunnel Corridor will improve access from the airport and the Dwarka Expressway to several of the capital's iconic destinations, including Qutub Minar, Mehrauli Archaeological Park, Hauz Khas Heritage Complex, Humayun's Tomb, Lodhi Garden and Chhatarpur Temple. It will also facilitate smoother travel to Bharat Mandapam, India Gate and other major venues that host international conferences, exhibitions and cultural events. By reducing congestion around the airport corridor and major traffic bottlenecks, the project will offer visitors a faster, more comfortable journey while supporting Delhi's hospitality, tourism and meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions (MICE) ecosystem. Strengthening Delhi's Global Gateway As the primary gateway to the National Capital, the Indira Gandhi International Airport serves millions of passengers each year. The new corridor will improve connectivity between the airport and Delhi's diplomatic enclave, business districts, convention centres and institutional hubs, enabling quicker and more predictable travel for international delegates, business travellers and investors. By strengthening links between the airport, Dwarka, Gurugram and South Delhi, the project will reinforce Delhi's position as a leading centre for commerce, diplomacy and global engagement. Building Sustainable Infrastructure A distinguishing feature of the project is its environmentally sensitive design. The 3.14-km twin-tube tunnel, including a 1.98-km section beneath the Southern Ridge, enables critical transport infrastructure to be developed while preserving Delhi's valuable green cover and minimising surface disruption. This approach reflects MoRTH's commitment to balancing infrastructure development with environmental stewardship. More than an urban road project, the Dwarka Tunnel Corridor represents a strategic investment in future-ready mobility. By improving connectivity, reducing congestion and integrating key transport corridors, it will enhance the quality of urban life, strengthen economic activity and support the continued growth of the National Capital Region. *** GDH/DS (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289390) आगंतुक पटल  : 155 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Tamil Ministry of Road Transport & Highways Delhi's Underground Link to the Future: The Tunnel Set to Rewire the Capital's Connectivity प्रविष्टि तिथि:
